description: Public edition: A coordinated portfolio of storage technologies matched to transportation, industry, buildings, and grid needs.
body:
High-Density Energy Storage Ecosystem. A coordinated portfolio of storage technologies matched to transportation, industry, buildings, and grid needs.

This database covers the technology as item 211 entry 45 of Manon's "100 Ultra-Advanced Future Technologies" catalog, section "Energy Beyond Conventional Infrastructure". It is the public edition: every factual claim below is drawn from real public science and engineering, honestly labeled.

Feasibility tier: demonstrated. Storage is deployed at scale: lithium-ion dominates, pumped hydro stores the most energy, and portfolios are standard utility practice.

Classification: public database. This record profiles the technology; companion records cover known science, constraints, approaches, tools, unresolved problems, evidence, and outlook.

title: High-Density Energy Storage Ecosystem - Known Science Foundations
description: Public edition: A coordinated portfolio of storage technologies matched to transportation, industry, buildings, and grid needs.
body:
Known science foundations of High-Density Energy Storage Ecosystem.

Lithium-ion pack prices fell ~90% since 2010. Pumped hydro holds ~95% of global storage energy. Grid batteries (Moss Landing, 3 GWh) firm renewables. Flow batteries, compressed air, thermal, and hydrogen storage cover other niches. Matching technology to application by duration and cycle life is established practice.

Key quantity check (Pumped hydro share of global storage energy / lithium-ion share): computed ratio 31.6667 against the reference value, relative error 0.001052, within the stated tolerance of 0.3. This calculation was executed in Node.js at build time and the output stored verbatim.

Nothing in this record is speculative: it reports established research, measurements, and validated methods.

title: High-Density Energy Storage Ecosystem - Physical and Engineering Constraints
description: Public edition: A coordinated portfolio of storage technologies matched to transportation, industry, buildings, and grid needs.
body:
Physical and engineering constraints on High-Density Energy Storage Ecosystem.

No single technology covers all durations and power needs. Long-duration storage economics are still difficult. Material supply chains (lithium, etc.) are constrained.

Scale analysis across 3 quantities spans 10.05 orders of magnitude; the dominant scale separation is global storage energy vs battery pack price decline at 10.05 orders of magnitude (global storage energy larger). Scale gaps this wide are the central engineering fact about this technology.

body:
Candidate approaches for High-Density Energy Storage Ecosystem, ranked by the weighted rubric 0.5*maturity - 0.25*cost - 0.25*risk:

1. Lithium-ion for short duration (maturity 5/5, cost 3/5, risk 1/5; score 1.5).

2. Flow batteries / LDES (maturity 3/5, cost 3/5, risk 2/5; score 0.25).

3. Thermal and hydrogen storage (maturity 3/5, cost 3/5, risk 2/5; score 0.25).

Top-ranked approach: Lithium-ion for short duration. Rankings are comparative planning aids, not predictions of success.

title: High-Density Energy Storage Ecosystem - Unresolved Problems
description: Public edition: A coordinated portfolio of storage technologies matched to transportation, industry, buildings, and grid needs.
body:
Unresolved problems for High-Density Energy Storage Ecosystem, in priority order (research burden index 17, 1 blocking):

Seasonal storage economics (severity 3/3, tractability 2/3, BLOCKING; priority 9).

Critical-mineral supply (severity 2/3, tractability 2/3; priority 4).

End-of-life recycling at scale (severity 2/3, tractability 2/3; priority 4).

These are open problems, stated plainly. A technology with unresolved blocking problems is not ready, whatever its promise.

body:
What would count as evidence of success for High-Density Energy Storage Ecosystem:

Portfolio meets a grid's full duration curve (weight 0.4; SATISFIED).

LDES reaches $20/kWh targets (weight 0.3; not yet satisfied).

Recycles 95% of battery materials (weight 0.3; not yet satisfied).
